text: A scope is the current value of role.default_scope and is not versioned: the change is one update under If-Match, the history of a scope is the decision record, and the service adds no version table and no valid-from or valid-to column.
why: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 gives role no version, valid-from or valid-to column, while the reference loads of this service are versioned; without a stated rule the app story would have to invent a column or a version table.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039) and T4 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS for a rule package version only); Architecture v5 slide 14 P4 OUT line; DP-15
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD003-APP sections 3, 4, 9, 11 and 13; RWB-P4-AD003-CON sections 4, 8 (BR7), 11 and 19
confirm: rwb-access service owner and the audit owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: Keeps the schema unchanged and puts the history in the decision record; a versioned scope would need a new table and a new approval rule

text: The scope read is GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/role-scopes and the scope change is PATCH /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/role-scopes/{roleCode}, with Platform administration R for the read and C for the change, an Idempotency-Key and an If-Match header on the change.
why: Neither the Ownership Map nor TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A gives a scope path, and the legacy key names no write endpoint, so the two operations this story needs have no path and no right from any source.
read: Ownership Map v1 api list (GET /admin/roles, GET /admin/access-log only); TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P4-007 (Platform administration, right R, scope applied); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (Platform administration: RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-AUDIT R); Template and Rules section R4 (base per service) and DP-13
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD003-APP sections 1, 3, 12.1 and 13; RWB-P4-AD003-CON sections 3, 11, 12.1 and 13
confirm: contract owner of rwb-access and the platform API review at the wave 4 contract freeze
impact: Gives the two operations a path and a right under the platform naming rule; a later map row or T-A row would supersede this path and would be a change to this baseline

text: A record outside the predicate is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 and never 403, no field of the record and no count of the excluded records is returned in any status, body, header or metric, and one decision-record entry with decision code AC-DENY and reason code OUT_OF_SCOPE is written through the library of DP-03; where the entry cannot be written the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and the record is not returned.
why: The legacy criterion says only that the system does not find the response and that the refusal is logged; the FSD fixes the 404 and the message, while no source fixes the entry's codes or the behaviour when the record cannot be written.
read: RWB-AD-003 AC2; FSD P4 v3 A2.14.3.1 VR-P4-014-1 (MSG-P4-003 This case is not in your scope.) and A2.14.4.3 AC-EXC-P4-014-01 (status 404 with message MSG-P4-003); RWB-AD-003 TC-AD-003-04 (A forced decision log write failure stops the action with MSG-P7-003); DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1037-CON error vocabulary

impact: Makes the refusal indistinguishable from an absence and always recorded; a 403 for an out-of-scope record is excluded by the assumption

text: A scope change is published as rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 on rwb.access.events.v1 with change kind SCOPE and the role code, the new scope value and the time; rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 is not used for it, and no third access event name exists.
why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-access exactly two events and names neither change kind; a scope change is an access-policy change and needs one signal for the services that cache permission data.
